Nike Inc. (NYSE:NKE) faces a more cautious Wall Street setup ahead of its fiscal first-quarter earnings report on Oct. 1, with several analysts cutting their price forecasts in recent days.

Nike carries a consensus Hold rating, with an average price forecast of $43.75.

Recent analyst actions include RBC Capital cutting its price forecast to $40 from $45 while maintaining a Sector Perform rating. Deutsche Bank lowered its forecast to $37 from $45 and kept a Hold rating, while Piper Sandler cut its forecast to $38 from $45 and maintained a Neutral rating.

Evercore ISI lowered its forecast to $34 from $46 with an In Line rating. Bank of America Securities downgraded Nike to Underperform and cut its forecast to $30 from $47.

Oppenheimer lowered its forecast to $52 from $60 while maintaining an Outperform rating, while Barclays cut its forecast to $48 from $52 and kept an Overweight rating.

RBC Sees Pressure on Revenue, China

RBC Capital Markets warned that the bigger risk may come from the company’s outlook rather than its first-quarter results.

Analyst Piral Dadhania said Nike’s current-quarter guidance is relatively tight, making a first-quarter miss less likely. However, investors will be focused on what management says about the coming quarters.

RBC expects first-quarter revenue of about $11.2 billion, down 4.3% year over year on a reported basis and 4.7% in constant currency. The firm forecasts diluted earnings of 43 cents per share.

The analyst expects North American revenue to fall 1% in constant currency, while Europe, the Middle East and Africa could decline 5%. Greater China remains the biggest pressure point, with RBC forecasting a 15% drop amid elevated inventories and discounting. Nike Direct revenue is expected to fall 8%.

RBC’s first-quarter revenue estimate is about 1% below consensus, while its EBIT forecast is 2% below Wall Street expectations.

RBC also expects Converse revenue to fall 25% in constant currency, saying the brand’s turnaround could take time as Nike rightsizes the business and aligns its cost base with weaker sales.

See More: Top Value Stocks

New CFO Could Reset Expectations

The analyst said Nike is making progress against its strategic goals, but the turnaround is taking longer than expected, with weak sell-through and elevated marketplace inventories still weighing on the recovery.

Dadhania said new CFO David Denton could reset expectations ahead of Nike’s capital markets day on Nov. 16-17. RBC also expects second-quarter guidance to point to another mid-single-digit revenue decline, even as gross margin improves.

The firm lowered its fiscal 2027 organic revenue growth forecast to a 3.1% decline from a previous 2% drop. RBC also cut its fiscal 2027 EBIT estimate by 3% and reduced its EPS forecast by 4% to $1.66.

Still, RBC sees some signs of improvement. Nike.com traffic has recovered from a low base, while newer products such as Pegasus Premium and Vomero 18 have generated stronger search interest. However, the analyst said marketplace inventories and promotional activity remain key hurdles to a broader recovery.

Nike Earnings Preview

Wall Street expects Nike to report earnings of 44 cents per share, down from 49 cents a year earlier.

Revenue is expected to fall to $11.33 billion from $11.72 billion in the year-ago quarter.

The estimates point to continued pressure on sales and profitability. Investors are likely to focus on gross margins, promotional activity, inventory levels, and management’s outlook.

Nike trades at about 17.1 times earnings, putting more emphasis on whether management can show tangible progress in its turnaround.

Nike Has Recently Beat Expectations

Nike has beaten earnings estimates in each of the past four quarters, with an average EPS surprise of about 54%.

In its most recent quarter, Nike reported earnings of 20 cents per share, beating the 13 cents estimate. Revenue of $10.97 billion also beat the $10.86 billion consensus estimate.

In December 2025, Nike reported earnings of 53 cents per share versus estimates of 38 cents. Revenue of $12.43 billion also beat expectations of $12.22 billion.

The recent track record shows Nike has repeatedly cleared Wall Street’s lowered expectations. However, with revenue and earnings expected to decline again, investors will likely focus on whether any upside comes from improving demand or mainly from cost controls.

NKE Price Action: Nike shares were down 0.18% at $35.77 at the time of publication on Wednesday. The stock is trading near its 52-week low of $35.21, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG) shares are popping Wednesday, bouncing off the stock’s 200-day moving average as a cluster of key averages appears to be acting as a support zone for the rally. Here’s what you should know.

  • Alphabet stock is showing exceptional strength. Why is GOOG stock up today?

Alphabet’s Chart Shows a Stock Working Through a Mid-Year Reset

Alphabet still looks like it’s in a longer-term uptrend working through a mid-year reset, with the stock up 42.60% over the past 12 months and trading 2.9% above its 200-day average of $337.14. In the near term, shares also sit 2.2% above the 20-day average of $339.47 and 1.6% above the 50-day average of $341.61.

The moving-average picture is somewhat mixed, with the 20-day average still below the 50-day, a near-term bearish signal, even as the 50-day holds above the 200-day, a more constructive longer-term setup. That combination often shows up when a stock is transitioning out of consolidation and back into a trend without having fully cleared its intermediate-term ceiling.

Today’s strength ties back to Alphabet finding support right at that 200-day average, a level sitting within a broader cluster of moving averages bunched close together. That tight grouping of technical levels can make moves feel fast once they get going, and today’s bounce looks like exactly that kind of move off a well-defined floor.

Anthropic’s IPO Filing Shows Heavy Reliance On Google Distribution

Separately, Anthropic’s confidential IPO prospectus, reviewed by Reuters, revealed the AI company routed 47% of its 2025 sales, or about $2.16 billion, through cloud partners Amazon and Google, underscoring how central Google’s platform has become to Anthropic’s distribution.

Anthropic paid the two cloud giants about $351 million in distribution fees over the same stretch, meaning roughly 16 cents of every dollar sold through their marketplaces flowed back to the platforms themselves.

The filing described the relationship as mutually beneficial, since Anthropic said offering its Claude models through Amazon, Google and Microsoft’s cloud platforms gives it access to customer bases it likely couldn’t reach on its own. Google and Amazon are both major investors in Anthropic and critical suppliers of the computing power behind its models, in addition to being distribution partners.

Anthropic’s reliance on the two companies has climbed steadily, with the share of revenue flowing through them jumping from just 11% in 2023 to 32% a year later and nearly half of all sales in 2025. The two companies also now collect 60% of Anthropic’s outstanding customer bills, up from 42% the year before.

GOOG Shares Are Jumping

AbbVie Inc. (NYSE:ABBV) announced clinical trial data on Wednesday for two pipeline candidates, highlighting progress in its immunology and metabolic disease portfolios.

The pharma giant shared encouraging Phase 2 outcomes for zumilokibart in treating moderate to severe atopic dermatitis, alongside promising Phase 1 weight-loss results for its novel amylin analog candidate, ABBV-295.

Read Also: AbbVie’s New Parkinson’s Pill Could Become a Billion-Dollar Drug, Analyst Says

Zumilokibart Shows Efficacy In Skin Condition Trial

In the Phase 2 APEX Part B study, 346 adult participants with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis received various doses of zumilokibart or placebo over 16 weeks.

Every evaluated dose achieved statistically significant improvements in skin clearance and itch reduction compared to placebo. High- and mid-dose regimens met key secondary endpoints, including EASI 90/100 skin clearance and I-NRS4 itch scores.

The mid-dose cohort demonstrated rapid skin severity reductions by Week 1 and itch relief by Week 2.

ABBV-295 Demonstrates Weight Loss Potential

Separately, AbbVie presented Phase 1 multiple ascending dose trial results for ABBV-295 at the European Association for the Study of Diabetes 2026 Annual Meeting.

The trial assessed the subcutaneous amylin analog—a drug class distinct from GLP-1 and GIP therapies—across 60 adults with a mean body mass index of 29.3 kg/m2.

Participants receiving ABBV-295 across once-weekly, biweekly, and monthly dosing schedules achieved dose-dependent body weight reductions ranging from -7.8% to -9.8% over 12 to 13 weeks, compared with a -0.3% change in the placebo group.

The drug’s mean half-life of 10.7 to 12.3 days supported extended dosing schedules. Adverse events were mostly mild, with no serious treatment-emergent events reported.

ABBV Price Action: AbbVie shares were up 0.16% to $263.71 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Super Micro Computer Inc‘s (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock price gained nearly 3% in Wednesday premarket trading but was last seen in the red as Nasdaq futures rose 0.34% and S&P 500 futures gained 0.38%.

The company’s premarket volume topped 1 million shares, compared with its three-month average daily volume of about 46 million.

Super Micro Expands Nvidia AI Infrastructure Push

Last week, Super Micro said that it was shipping Nvidia Corp‘s (NASDAQ:NVDA) Vera Rubin NVL72 racks with direct liquid cooling, networking, storage, power and deployment services designed to scale from 5-megawatt installations to gigawatt-scale data centers.

Management continues to see strong AI demand, with a roughly $60 billion order book supporting its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook of $65 billion to $72 billion.

However, margin pressure, corporate governance concerns and shareholder dilution remain key investor risks.

HPE Lands $1.2 Billion AMD Helios Order

Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. (NYSE:HPE) secured a $1.2 billion order from Vultr to deploy Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) Helios AI Rack by HPE systems across U.S. cloud data centers.

The agreement marks HPE’s first order for the new platform. Each system combines 72 AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs, EPYC "Venice" CPUs, Pensando networking and ROCm software, while HPE supplies Juniper-based networking, direct liquid cooling and deployment services.

HPE CEO Antonio Neri said, "AI is driving the largest infrastructure buildout in history and together with AMD and Vultr, we are building an open foundation to accelerate the next phase of AI."

The order highlights increasing competition among infrastructure vendors to provide integrated compute, networking and cooling systems for large AI deployments.

Analysts Remain Cautious On Super Micro

Super Micro carries a Hold consensus rating with an average price forecast of $39.50.

Citigroup maintained a Neutral rating and raised its forecast to $39 on Aug. 12. Goldman Sachs maintained a Sell rating while lifting its forecast to $34, while Mizuho maintained Neutral and raised its forecast to $35.

ETFs Hold Meaningful Super Micro Exposure

The iShares Future AI & Tech ETF (NYSE:ARTY) holds a 4.40% weighting in Super Micro, while the iShares US Digital Infrastructure and Real Estate ETF (NYSE:IDGT) holds 4.94% and the ERShares Entrepreneurs ETF (NASDAQ:ENTR) holds 3.74%.

Significant inflows or outflows from these funds can translate into buying or selling of Super Micro shares.

Price Action

Super Micro Computer shares were down 0.67% at $40.74 at last check on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo on Tuesday said the CLARITY Act’s collapse came down to pure politics, not any irreconcilable policy dispute.

Politics, Not Policy, Killed the Bill

Cuomo told Bloomberg Television said the bill had the best name of any recent legislation because it was actually about clarity. 

“When CLARITY failed, ambiguity wins and unpredictability wins,” he said, adding that’s exactly what the crypto industry can’t tolerate. 

He argued no differences in the bill were irreconcilable, framing the failure entirely as election-year maneuvering. 

“There are no right reasons for that bill to fail,” Cuomo said, expressing hope a lame-duck Congress could still pass it once political temperatures cool after the midterms.

Cuomo pointed to his own record, having passed New York’s BitLicense framework in 2015 as one of the first state-level crypto regulatory regimes. 

He acknowledged the license became too stringent over time, pushing companies like Kraken and Bitfinex out of the state, but defended its original goal of pairing innovation with consumer protection.

Why Cuomo Expects a Republican Wave to Reverse

Cuomo compared this cycle to 1994, when Democrats lost the House and Senate two years after Clinton’s election, calling the historical midterm pattern “more pronounced now.” 

He argued voters aren’t necessarily endorsing the Democratic platform but are seeking balance after two years of Republican dominance. 

“They’re saying the Democratic socialist agenda blows us away,” he said, distinguishing that energy from broader national appeal, which he doesn’t believe extends beyond major cities.

Cuomo said the crypto industry failed to mobilize its own voter base during the CLARITY Act debate, despite tens of millions of Americans holding crypto. 

“Where were they in the debate about the CLARITY Act? Where are they as a political force?” he asked, arguing the industry can’t simply rely on political donations to pass legislation.

Why Regulation Can’t Replace Legislation

Cuomo also warned that SEC and CFTC rulemaking filling the gap left by CLARITY’s failure remains vulnerable if Congress changes hands. 

He said that regulations can be challenged, investigated, and undone far more easily than actual law, which would add more chaos to the system rather than the clarity the industry actually needs.

Why This Ties Into Bitcoin’s Midterm Pattern

Cuomo’s read on the political mood lines up with a separate concern already circulating in crypto markets. 

As Benzinga reported Tuesday, analyst Ali Martinez flagged that Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) has fallen sharply after every midterm election since 2010. 

The weak Republican approval numbers Cuomo cited only add to that uncertainty heading into Nov. 3.

Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ:FFAI) is no longer presenting itself simply as an EV maker with a robotics side business. The El Segundo, California-based company is proposing a broader Physical AI holding-company model inspired by Berkshire Hathaway Inc (NYSE:BRK) (NYSE:BRK) and Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG), while moving its robotics operation into FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ:FFR) and pursuing robotaxi operations.

The Tesla Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA) connection could make that restructuring more consequential.

A Portfolio of Physical AI

Faraday Future says it plans to become a Physical AI investment, incubation and holding company, combining industrial operations with capital investment. The strategy would let mature businesses develop independently while FFAI retains an ownership stake.

Read Also: FFR Robotics Stock Gets a New Nasdaq Identity

The first major example is its robotics business, which recently combined with AIxCrypto Holdings Inc (NASDAQ:AIXC), and was renamed FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc., with ticker symbol FFR. The transaction carries an estimated $200 million valuation, subject to definitive agreements, approvals and regulatory requirements.

“FFAI plans to adopt an upgraded operating model inspired by Berkshire Hathaway and Alphabet,” the company stated in its press release.

That structure is where the Berkshire Hathaway comparison comes in. Rather than keeping every business under one operating company, FFAI says it wants to incubate businesses, allow them to mature and potentially unlock their value through separate listings or operations.

The Alphabet comparison points to using a parent structure to house businesses built around different technologies. Faraday’s portfolio would focus on Physical AI, spanning robotics, mobility and related technologies.

Tesla Creates the Twist

Faraday Future says it plans to upgrade FFAI from an EV manufacturer into a robotaxi shared-operations company, working with RoboShare on vehicle onboarding, operations and user services. It also plans to explore connecting its vehicles to Tesla’s Cybercab network.

That does not amount to a Tesla partnership. It is Faraday Future’s stated plan to have “potential connectivity with the Cybercab network.”

For investors, the strategy is less about competing with Tesla and more about finding a place inside a market Tesla is helping build.

The company is also exploring its EAI cabin technology for other intelligent vehicles, while RoboShare provides the shared-mobility infrastructure. That gives FFAI another potential route to participate in autonomous transportation without relying solely on its own vehicle sales.

What Investors Should Watch

The FFR transaction is new, and Faraday’s robotaxi plans depend on execution, financing, regulatory approvals and the development of its shared-mobility operations. The company itself flags substantial funding, regulatory and execution risks in its disclosures.

But the restructuring changes the investment question. FFAI is trying to shift from a company centered on its automotive operation to a holding platform with stakes in robotics, robotaxis, and Physical AI.

Investors should watch whether that structure produces independently valuable businesses and whether the Tesla-connected robotaxi strategy becomes an actual operating opportunity.

Shares of Capricor Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ:CAPR) are trading higher Wednesday morning following the release of positive long-term clinical data for its lead cellular therapy. The rally provides critical support for the biotechnology firm as it attempts to salvage a regulatory approval following a recent advisory panel rejection.

Here’s what investors need to know.

  • Capricor Therapeutics stock is charging ahead with explosive momentum. What’s fueling CAPR momentum?

HOPE-3 Data Backs Revised BLA Strategy

Late Tuesday, Capricor announced 24-month results from its pivotal Phase 3 HOPE-3 trial evaluating deramiocel in patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD).The data demonstrated that the cell therapy sharply slowed the decline of upper-limb function compared to a placebo over the two-year evaluation period.

The functional preservation data is central to Capricor’s revised commercial pathway. The findings directly support the core efficacy metrics currently under review by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the drug’s amended Biologics License Application.

Following the clinical results, B. Riley upgraded Capricor from Neutral to Buy on Wednesday morning, raising its price target on the stock from $5 to $21.

Rebounding from Regulatory Setbacks

Wednesday’s momentum marks a reversal in sentiment after Capricor shares lost a majority of their value in late July. The steep sell-off was triggered when an FDA Advisory Committee voted against recommending approval for deramiocel for its originally targeted indication of DMD-related cardiomyopathy.

Following the negative panel vote, Capricor narrowed the scope of its BLA to focus explicitly on preserving upper-limb function in DMD patients. To accommodate the review of the newly submitted 24-month HOPE-3 data and the amended clinical indication, the FDA subsequently extended the drug’s PDUFA target action date to Nov. 22.

While regulatory risks remain elevated heading into the November decision, analysts note that the late-breaking upper-limb efficacy data provides the fundamental clinical backing necessary to support the revised application.

CAPR Stock Surges Wednesday

CAPR Price Action: Capricor Therapeutics shares were up 11.79% at $9.59 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.
